args.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks

# Load data from file_ids
# files[0]['table'] contains the columns
x = files[0]['table']['raman_shift_cm-1']
y = files[0]['table']['intensity']

# Normalization (Min-Max)
y_min, y_max = np.min(y), np.max(y)
if y_max - y_min != 0:
    y_norm = (y - y_min) / (y_max - y_min)
else:
    y_norm = y - y_min

# Peak detection on normalized data
# Use a relative height threshold to avoid noise
peaks, properties = find_peaks(y_norm, height=0.05, distance=10)
peak_x = x[peaks]
peak_y = y_norm[peaks]

# Save the normalized spectrum
save_result('T093_normalized', y_norm, raman_shift=x)

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.subplot(2, 1, 1)
plt.plot(x, y, color='blue')
plt.title('Original Spectrum T093')
plt.ylabel('Intensity (a.u.)')
plt.grid(True)

plt.subplot(2, 1, 2)
plt.plot(x, y_norm, color='green')
plt.plot(peak_x, peak_y, 'rx')
plt.title('Normalized Spectrum T093 with Detected Peaks')
plt.xlabel('Raman Shift (cm-1)')
plt.ylabel('Normalized Intensity')
plt.grid(True)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print(f"Original intensity range: {y_min:.2f} to {y_max:.2f}")
print(f"Number of peaks detected: {len(peaks)}")
for px, py in zip(peak_x, peak_y):
    print(f"Peak at {px:.2f} cm-1 with normalized intensity {py:.3f}")
